name: ZeroSSL
titleTag: ZeroSSL alternative for Let's Encrypt | docstoc
metaDescription: ZeroSSL sells its own certificates and a dedicated dashboard. docstoc runs Let's Encrypt DV inside your workspace. See what each does and costs.
headline: ZeroSSL or docstoc: a certificate authority or an automation layer
sub: ZeroSSL is a certificate authority with its own console: docstoc manages Let's Encrypt certificates beside your invoices and documents.
whatItIs: ZeroSSL is a certificate authority with a control panel, ACME support, monitoring and a REST API. Its pricing page lists a free plan with 3 certificates of 90 days, and paid plans that add annual certificates and annual wildcards. It suits people who want a dedicated place to order, track and automate certificates, from a single site to a larger set of domains.
whereTheyAreStronger: ZeroSSL issues certificates itself, including 1-year certificates on paid plans. docstoc only issues 90-day Let's Encrypt certificates.
Paid plans list unlimited 90-day certificates. docstoc caps every plan at 5 certificate slots.
ZeroSSL offers monitoring and a REST API as part of its core feature list, and lists several validation methods. docstoc validates by DNS only.
Higher plans include several annual wildcards. docstoc Business includes one wildcard.
whereDocstocFits: Free gives you 5 Let's Encrypt certificates of 90 days, against 3 on ZeroSSL's free plan at the time of writing.
Certificates live in the same workspace as your chase drafts, document templates and file certificates, so there is one login.
Validation is always DNS-01: you publish one TXT record and click verify. There is no email or file-upload path to choose between.
docstoc is an automation layer, not a certificate seller. Let's Encrypt issues the certificate and you do not buy a certificate product.

comparison.docstoc: Let's Encrypt. docstoc manages the ACME order for domains you control.

comparison.competitor: 3 certificates of 90 days on the Free plan, at the time of writing.
comparison.docstoc: 5 certificates of 90 days on Free.

comparison.competitor: Basic from $14.99 a month up to Platinum at $219.99 a month, at the time of writing.
comparison.docstoc: Pro $14.99 a month and Business $39.99 a month, covering the whole workspace and not only SSL.

comparison.competitor: 90-day and annual certificates, with annual wildcards on higher plans.
comparison.docstoc: 90-day DV only. One wildcard on Business.

comparison.competitor: ACME clients renew unattended.
comparison.docstoc: docstoc sends a reminder email about 30 days before expiry. You then open the app, click Renew, publish a new DNS TXT value and verify. Renewal is a guided manual step, not unattended.

whenToChoose.competitor: Choose ZeroSSL if you want a dedicated certificate console, annual certificates, several wildcards, or an ACME client that renews without your involvement. It is the better fit for a set of domains that changes often.
whenToChoose.docstoc: Choose docstoc if you run a handful of hostnames, already use it for invoice chasing or documents, and are happy to renew each certificate by hand every few months with a reminder to prompt you.

faq.q: Is docstoc a replacement for ZeroSSL?
faq.a: Only for simple needs. docstoc issues Let's Encrypt DV certificates with a guided DNS step, but it does not issue annual certificates and renewal is not unattended. If you rely on ACME automation, ZeroSSL or a standard ACME client fits better.

faq.q: Can I move my ZeroSSL certificate into docstoc?
faq.a: No, you issue a new one. docstoc never takes a private key. Add the hostname, publish the DNS TXT record, verify, then switch your host to the new certificate and let the ZeroSSL one lapse.

faq.q: How many free certificates do I get?
faq.a: docstoc Free includes 5 certificates of 90 days, one hostname each. ZeroSSL's pricing page lists 3 on its Free plan at the time of writing. Check both pages before you decide, since limits change.

sources.supports: Plans, prices and limits: Free 3 90-day certs; Basic $14.99, Premium $68.99, Business $129.99, Platinum $219.99 per month; annual certificates and wildcards on paid plans; ACME on all plans
Feature list: control panel, ACME, monitoring, REST API, multiple validation methods, CA role

existingClaimIssues: Existing page says Free 'includes 5 x 90-day' and 'renewals in-product' and compares with 'auto-renew'. Renewal is guided manual (new TXT per renewal).

Several existing pages say 'auto-renew' or 'renewals in-product' (zerossl, digicert, sectigo, letsencrypt 'leave it for renewals'). name: Let's Encrypt
metaDescription: Let's Encrypt is free and run by a nonprofit. docstoc uses it too and adds a guided DNS workflow. See when DIY is enough and when it is not.
headline: Let's Encrypt on your own or through docstoc
sub: Same certificate authority: the question is who runs the ACME client and how much you want to click.
whatItIs: Let's Encrypt is a free, automated and open certificate authority, operated by the nonprofit Internet Security Research Group. It issues Domain Validation certificates only, valid for 90 days, with an opt-in six-day option. You run an ACME client on your own server or use one built into your host, and it renews the certificate by itself. Support comes from documentation and community forums.
whereTheyAreStronger: Let's Encrypt is free and docstoc is not. If you can run certbot or a host-integrated client, you pay nothing.
A good ACME client renews unattended every 60 days or so. docstoc asks you to renew by hand.
Let's Encrypt offers six-day certificates as an option. docstoc issues 90-day certificates only.
There is no certificate slot cap on the CA side. docstoc limits each plan to 5 certificates.
whereDocstocFits: You do not install or maintain an ACME client. docstoc generates the order and shows the exact TXT name and value.
DNS-01 works when the site is not live yet or sits behind a CDN, and it is the only route for wildcards.
Certificates, expiry dates and reminders sit with your invoices and documents in one workspace.
Free covers 5 certificates, which suits a small business with a few hostnames and no sysadmin.

comparison.competitor: Free certificates.
comparison.docstoc: Free for 5 certificates, then Pro at $14.99 a month or Business at $39.99 a month for the whole workspace.

comparison.competitor: You, with certbot or another client, or your host.
comparison.docstoc: docstoc runs the order. You publish the TXT record and click verify.

comparison.competitor: Clients renew about every 60 days, automatically.
comparison.docstoc: docstoc sends a reminder email about 30 days before expiry. You then open the app, click Renew, publish a new DNS TXT value and verify. Renewal is a guided manual step, not unattended.

comparison.competitor: HTTP-01, DNS-01 and others. Wildcards need DNS-01.
comparison.docstoc: DNS-01 only.

comparison.competitor: Documentation and community forums, no direct support.
comparison.docstoc: Email support at founder@docstoc.io.

whenToChoose.competitor: Choose Let's Encrypt directly if you already run an ACME client or your host offers one. It costs nothing, renews itself and is the standard route for servers you control.
whenToChoose.docstoc: Choose docstoc if nobody on the team wants to maintain certbot, you manage few hostnames, and a reminder plus a few clicks every quarter is acceptable to you.

faq.q: Are docstoc certificates real Let's Encrypt certificates?
faq.a: Yes. docstoc is an automation layer on Let's Encrypt and does not resell another authority's certificates. The browser padlock is the same as a certificate you get through certbot.

faq.q: Do docstoc certificates renew automatically?
faq.a: No. Renewal is guided: you get a reminder about 30 days before expiry, click Renew, publish a new TXT value and verify. If you want unattended renewal, run an ACME client yourself.

faq.q: Do I need docstoc if my host already gives me HTTPS?
faq.a: No. If your host provisions Let's Encrypt for you, you already have what docstoc offers. docstoc helps when you manage the DNS yourself or need a wildcard.

name: DigiCert
titleTag: DigiCert alternative for simple HTTPS | docstoc
metaDescription: DigiCert sells OV and EV certificates with CertCentral. docstoc automates free Let's Encrypt DV. See the limits of each before you switch.
headline: DigiCert for verified identity, docstoc for a plain padlock
sub: DigiCert sells organisation-validated certificates and a management platform: docstoc only issues domain-validated ones.
whatItIs: DigiCert sells TLS certificates in organisation validated (OV) and extended validation (EV) tiers, with single-domain, multi-domain and wildcard coverage. Its certificate pages describe the CertCentral management portal, DigiCert ONE and Trust Lifecycle Manager. It is built for organisations that need verified company details in the certificate and central control over many certificates.
whereTheyAreStronger: DigiCert issues OV and EV certificates that carry a verified organisation. docstoc cannot issue either.
Its Basic tier lists unlimited issuance and replacement, free ACME automation and CertCentral.
Higher tiers add priority order processing, domain reputation monitoring and brand protection through certificate transparency log monitoring.
DigiCert ONE and Trust Lifecycle Manager cover discovery and lifecycle control at a scale docstoc does not attempt.
whereDocstocFits: If you only need HTTPS on a marketing site or portal, domain validation is what docstoc issues, and Free covers 5 certificates.
Paid plans start at $14.99 a month for the whole workspace, against DigiCert's OV list prices from $372 a year per domain at the time of writing.
Setup is one DNS TXT record. There is no organisation vetting to wait for.
Certificates sit beside invoice chasing, templates and file certificates in one login.

whenToChoose.competitor: Choose DigiCert if your customers, auditors or procurement rules call for a verified organisation name, if you manage many certificates centrally, or if you need EV or a vendor-backed support relationship.
whenToChoose.docstoc: Choose docstoc if all you need is a working HTTPS certificate on a few hostnames, you accept that it names only the domain, and you want it in the same workspace as your other business paperwork.

faq.q: Can docstoc replace my DigiCert OV certificate?
faq.a: No. docstoc issues domain validated certificates only, so the certificate will not carry your organisation's verified details. If a contract or policy requires OV or EV, stay with a commercial authority.

faq.q: Is a Let's Encrypt certificate less secure than a DigiCert one?
faq.a: Not in encryption terms. Both secure the connection. The difference is the identity checking: DV proves control of a domain, OV and EV also check the organisation. Whether that matters depends on your requirements.

faq.q: How do I switch a hostname from DigiCert to docstoc?
faq.a: Issue the new certificate first, install it on your host, check HTTPS, then let the DigiCert order lapse. docstoc never takes a private key, so the old key is not moved.

name: Cloudflare
metaDescription: Cloudflare Universal SSL is free for proxied hostnames on Cloudflare. docstoc issues Let's Encrypt certificates for hosts you run yourself.
headline: Cloudflare Universal SSL or a certificate you install yourself
sub: Cloudflare's certificate sits at its edge for proxied records: docstoc gives you a certificate and key to install on your own server.
whatItIs: Cloudflare Universal SSL issues free, unshared, publicly trusted domain validated certificates for domains that are active on Cloudflare, on every plan. Cloudflare renews them automatically and, for proxied DNS records, serves the certificate at its edge. It picks the authority itself, among Let's Encrypt, Google Trust Services and SSL.com. It suits sites that already use Cloudflare's proxy and DNS.
whereTheyAreStronger: Universal SSL is free on every Cloudflare plan and renews automatically with nothing for you to do.
The certificate is served at Cloudflare's edge for proxied records, so you install nothing on your origin to get HTTPS for visitors.
It sits inside a wider platform with DNS, caching and security, which docstoc does not provide.
Advanced Certificate Manager and custom certificates exist for deeper subdomains, cipher suites and a chosen authority.
whereDocstocFits: You get a PEM certificate and key to install on a server you control, which is what you need when the origin or a mail server must present its own certificate.
It works with any DNS provider. You publish a TXT record where your DNS already lives, including Cloudflare DNS.
You can request a wildcard on Business, validated by DNS-01.
Certificates, expiry dates and reminders sit next to your invoices and documents.

comparison.competitor: Free on all plans for domains active on Cloudflare.
comparison.docstoc: Free for 5 certificates; paid plans from $14.99 a month.

whenToChoose.competitor: Choose Cloudflare if your domain already runs through its proxy. Universal SSL is free, automatic and needs no installation, which is hard to beat for a standard website.
whenToChoose.docstoc: Choose docstoc if you need a certificate you hold and install yourself, for a server that is not proxied, and you are fine renewing it with a guided DNS step.

faq.q: Do I need Cloudflare to use docstoc SSL?
faq.a: No. docstoc works with whichever DNS provider you use, as long as you can add a TXT record. You may keep Cloudflare for DNS and still get a certificate from docstoc.

faq.q: Is Cloudflare Universal SSL really free?
faq.a: Yes, on every plan, for domains that are active on Cloudflare. Cloudflare serves it only for proxied records. For DNS-only records your origin must provide its own certificate.

faq.q: Why would I need a separate certificate if I use Cloudflare?
faq.a: Usually to run HTTPS on the origin itself, or on a hostname that is not proxied. Then you need a certificate on the server, and a Let's Encrypt one from docstoc or a client of your own does that.

titleTag: SSL For Free alternative with a workspace | docstoc
metaDescription: SSL For Free is a front end to ZeroSSL certificates. docstoc runs Let's Encrypt with DNS validation in one workspace. See how they differ.
headline: SSL For Free or docstoc: a ZeroSSL front end or Let's Encrypt in a workspace
sub: SSL For Free hands out ZeroSSL certificates in a web form: docstoc issues Let's Encrypt certificates and keeps them with your business paperwork.
whatItIs: SSL For Free is a web service powered by ZeroSSL. It issues certificates through ACME (free 90-day certificates) or a web app and REST API, with email, HTTP and DNS verification. Its page says the private key is generated and encrypted on your device and downloaded only through your logged-in browser. It lists a free plan with 3 certificates and paid plans from $13.99 a month.
whereTheyAreStronger: It offers email, HTTP and DNS verification, so you can validate without touching DNS. docstoc uses DNS only.
The key is generated and encrypted on your device per the page, so the service does not hold a usable copy of it.
Paid plans list unlimited 90-day certificates and 1-year certificates. docstoc has a 5-slot cap and 90-day certificates only.
It names ACME access on paid plans for fully automated renewal with clients such as Certbot.
whereDocstocFits: Free covers 5 certificates, against 3 on SSL For Free's listed free plan at the time of writing.
You publish one DNS TXT record and verify. No file upload and no email alias.
Certificates, expiry reminders, invoices, templates and file certificates share one login.
Pro at $14.99 a month and Business at $39.99 cover the whole workspace, not only SSL.

whenToChoose.competitor: Choose SSL For Free if you want a quick web form, HTTP or email validation, annual certificates, or a larger number of wildcards, and you are happy with ZeroSSL behind it.
whenToChoose.docstoc: Choose docstoc if you manage a few hostnames, prefer DNS validation, and want certificates in the same account as invoice chasing and documents, with a reminder-led renewal.

faq.q: Is SSL For Free the same as ZeroSSL?
faq.a: Closely related. SSL For Free's page says it is powered by ZeroSSL, which provides the infrastructure, and paid plans are sign-ups on ZeroSSL's app. docstoc is separate and uses Let's Encrypt.

faq.q: Which gives more free certificates?
faq.a: docstoc Free includes 5 certificates of 90 days; SSL For Free lists 3 on its free plan at the time of writing. Check both pages, as plans change.

faq.q: Do I have to renew a docstoc certificate by hand?
faq.a: Yes. You get a reminder about 30 days before expiry, click Renew, publish a new TXT value and verify. SSL For Free recommends automating renewal with ZeroSSL ACME or Certbot.
